podcast.title: Attempt to Revive Gamma Ray
podcast.body: After his work with Screaming Trees and the first Desert Sessions, Josh Homme considered resurrecting his Gamma Ray project for a new long-term endeavor. However, a German power metal band already held the name and threatened legal action, forcing him to choose a different name. "His first thought was to resurrect gamma ray, but there was a problem. A German power metal band had dibs on that name and started making noises about legal action."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Desert Session Projects – Produced by Eleven Members
podcast.body: Josh Homme's Desert Session projects received production assistance from Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider of the band Eleven, following their work on Chris Cornell's solo album. This collaboration brought Johannes and Schneider into contact with members from various other prominent bands, including A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects, which brought them into contact with members of a perfect circle, nine-inch nails, Danzig, Wade, Maryland Manson's band, and PJ Harvey."

podcast.title: Early Band Practice Locations
podcast.body: During his time with Cats and Jammer, Josh Homme recalls practicing in garages in the high desert that were later converted into meth labs at night. "Josh remembers practicing in garages that were later converted into meth labs at night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Musical Beginnings
podcast.body: Born into a well-to-do family in the high desert east of Palm Springs, California, where his father worked as a contractor in the Coachella Valley. Josh initially wanted to play drums, but his parents encouraged him to learn a "real instrument," leading him to acquire his first $50 acoustic guitar at age 10. "Josh Ami, who is the only continuous member of Queens of the Stone Age, was a kid from a well to do family. Dad was a contractor who built houses in the Coachella Valley. Josh first wanted to play drums, but Mum and Dad insisted that he learn a real instrument."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Early Music Lessons
podcast.body: His initial formal music training involved learning to play polkas on the guitar, a venture that lasted only about two weeks before he discovered the raw energy of hardcore punk. "The first thing Josh learned how to play were polkas. That lasted about two weeks before he discovered hardcore punk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Early Polka Guitar Lessons
podcast.body: At the age of nine, when Josh Homme first began learning to play the guitar, he took polka lessons. This unexpected musical foundation precedes his later fame as a guitarist known for his distinct rock style. "When Josh Hommie of Queens of the Stone Age first wanted to learn how to play the guitar at the age of nine, he took polka lessons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Guitar Sound Secrecy
podcast.body: Josh Homme is famously protective of the specifics of how he achieves his guitar sound, carefully guarding his techniques. "And by the way, do not ask Josh about how he gets his guitar sound. He guards it very, very carefully."

podcast.title: Post-Kyuss Musical Influences
podcast.body: Following the breakup of Kyuss, Homme's musical direction was significantly influenced by his discovery of albums like Iggy Pop's "Lust for Life" and "The Idiot," steering him towards a new sound distinct from Kyuss's. "It was around this time that Josh discovered albums like Lust for Life and the Idiot. That was the kind of music he wanted to make now, not whatever Kaya's was doing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Producer for Arctic Monkeys' AM
podcast.body: Josh Homme, a professional producer known for his work with Queens of the Stone Age, worked with Arctic Monkeys on their album "AM". This collaboration marked the first time Arctic Monkeys used a professional producer, significantly elevating the quality of their music. "concretamente el de Queen's of the Stone Age, trabajando con Joe's Home [Josh Homme], la música de los artichmonks llegó a un nivel de calidad que jamás no sabíamos imaginado."

podcast.title: Screaming Trees Tour as Guitarist
podcast.body: Josh Homme spent two years touring as the rhythm guitarist for the Seattle band Screaming Trees after meeting their singer Mark Lanegan, a Kyuss fan. He was described as a six-foot-five red-haired rhythm guitarist during their Lollapalooza 1996 set. "Mark was a fan of Kaya's and needed someone to tour with the trees and ask Josh if he would like to be his guitarist. So he did that for two years. If you were at Lollapalooza in 1996 and saw the tree set, that six foot five red-haired rhythm guitarist was Josh Hommie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Seattle Hiatus and Education
podcast.body: After his Gamma Ray project, Homme sought a change of scenery from the desert, moving to Seattle in 1996 and 1997. During this period, he took a break from music to study business at the University of Washington. "He needed a change of scenery from the desert. So he moved to Seattle, a very wet place to do nothing. The idea was to take a break from music and go back to school. And he did that for 1996 and 1997. He studied business at the University of Washington."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Secrets of Queens of the Stone Age: Part 1

podcast.title: Unique Guitar Strumming Style
podcast.body: Homme's distinctive guitar playing style is attributed to a combination of the straight up and down strumming techniques found in hardcore punk bands like GBH and Discharge, integrated with the strumming required for playing polkas. "You combine that with the strumming required to play polkas, and you suddenly begin to understand why Josh plays guitar the way he does, and why Queens of the Stone Age sounds just a little bit different."

xref.title: Breakup in 1995
xref.body: Kyuss broke up in October 1995, with the lineup consisting of Josh Homme, Scott Reeder on bass, Fredo Hernandez on drums, and John Garcia on vocals. The breakup appeared amicable, largely due to boredom and a desire by members like Josh Homme (who was 21 at the time, having started when he was 17) to explore other musical avenues. "And then suddenly, out of nowhere, in October of 1995, caes broke up. At the time, the group consisted of Josh, Scott Reader on bass, drummer Fredo Hernandez, and singer John Garcia. The breakup seemed to be fairly friendly. Everybody just seemed to be bored. It was time."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri's Firing (2004)
xref.body: Bassist Nick Oliveri was fired by Josh Homme in 2004, primarily due to his "loose cannon" behavior, disrespect for fans, and "crazy partying" during the "Songs for the Deaf" tour in Australia. Other factors included aggression towards Homme over his then-girlfriend Brody Dalle, and Homme's suspicion that Oliveri was physically abusing his girlfriend. "All of a very was fired for disrespecting the group's fans, not to mention the crazy partying."

xref.title: Nick Oliveri's Firing (Early 2004)
xref.body: Bassist Nick Oliveri was fired by Josh Homme in early 2004 due to a series of "incidents occurring over the last 18 months." These included being arrested in Brazil for public nudity (performing in only sneakers), getting the band banned from a hotel in Australia, and, most critically, throwing full Corona beer bottles at the audience during a gig, pitched like fastballs. "A number of incidents occurring over the last 18 months have led to the decision that the two can no longer maintain a working partnership in the band."

xref.title: 2010 Surgical Incident and Clinical Death
xref.body: In the fall of 2010, Josh Homme underwent surgery on his leg (not a knee operation as misreported). During the procedure, he was incorrectly intubated, choked under anesthesia, and stopped breathing. He flatlined on the operating table and was officially dead for a couple of minutes before being revived with a defibrillator. "What we do know, though, is that Josh was incorrectly intubated and ended up choking at in the anesthesia, and he stopped breathing. Before he could be revived with a defibrillator, he flatlined there on the operating table and was officially dead for a couple of minutes before he could be revived with a defibrillator."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: People Who (Almost) Died

xref.title: Josh Homme's Near-Death Experience (Fall 2010)
xref.body: In the fall of 2010, Josh Homme underwent a routine knee operation that led to a critical intubation error. This caused him to asphyxiate, and his heart stopped, resulting in full cardiac arrest, from which he was revived with a defibrillator. During his 13-day hospital stay, he contracted MRSA, a dangerous superbug, in his leg, leading to four months of being bedridden, extreme pain, disorientation, and isolation from his young daughter, Camille, which severely impacted his mental health and creative drive. "He started to asphyxiate. First he stopped breathing, then his heart stopped beating. Full cardiac arrest."

xref.body: Josh Homme was not present at the Bataclan theater in Paris on November 13, 2015, when terrorists attacked an Eagles of Death Metal concert, resulting in the deaths of 89 people, due to his flexible touring schedule with the band. "That's why he wasn't at the Bataclan theater in Paris when terrorists took over the place on November 13th, 2015 and killed 89 people who were all at an Eagles of Deathmale show."

xref.title: "Free Tag 415" Tattoo

"It was so bad that each member of the group got that tattoo to remind them to never perform that poorly ever again."

Dave Grohl stepped in to assist with the remaining drum sessions for the album "...Like Clockwork." "Long time drummer Joey Castillo was fired during this time. xref.title: Band Naming Origin
xref.body: The name "Queens of the Stone Age" originated from producer Chris Goss, a member of Masters of Reality, who would jokingly refer to Kyuss as "Queens of the Stone Age" during studio sessions, suggesting they sounded like royal women of the Stone Age. Josh Homme found the phrase cool and funny, especially imagining it on a marquee or concert ticket, leading him to adopt it for his new project. "Whenever he was in the studio with the band, he would yell at Kias, calling them Queens of the Stone Age. As in you guys all sound like Queens of the Stone Age."

xref.title: Distinctive Guitar Sound
xref.body: Kyuss developed a unique sound by tuning guitars down as low as possible, to the point where the strings were floppy. Josh Homme further enhanced this by running his guitar through both guitar and bass amps and cabinets, making the low end particularly prominent. "The guitars were tuned down as low as possible, right to the point where the strings were so floppy that they couldn't be played. The sounds that came out seemed to appeal to the stoners in the crowd, so they went with that."

xref.title: Healing Process and Return to Music
xref.body: It took Josh Homme a couple of years to mentally recover from his traumatic experiences, utilizing meditation as part of his healing. He was cleared to walk again in December 2010, and by January 2011, he began working on a new Queens of the Stone Age album, though he initially struggled as his "heart just wasn't in it." "It took a couple of years to sort out his head. He created his meditation as being part of the healing process. The depression he says was absolutely intense. Eventually, Josh got back to being something of his old self. He was clear to start walking again in December 2010, and in January 2011, he started working on a new Queen's of the Stone Age album."

xref.body: Following his 2010 surgery and MRSA infection, Josh Homme experienced a profound period of mental and creative struggle. For a couple of years, he lost the ability to hear music in his head, a constant presence since childhood, which greatly affected him. xref.title: Musical Direction Shift
xref.body: After Kyuss, Josh Homme aimed for a "clean slate" with Queens of the Stone Age, desiring a sound that was shorter, sharper, tighter, cleaner, and more focused, consciously moving away from the long stoner rock jams of his previous band. "Josh wanted a clean slate, so no more long-stone or rock jams. It said to be shorter, sharper, tighter, cleaner, and with more focus."

xref.title: Musical Influence and Genre Pioneering
xref.body: Kyuss was highly influential, considered "ground zero" for a new form of fuzzy guitar music. They were credited with pioneering genres known as Desert Rock, Dirt Rock, and particularly Stoner Rock, a term Josh Homme personally disliked. "They were ground zero of a new form of fuzzy guitar music. Some called it Desert Rock. You can see why. And others used the term Dirt Rock. But the one that really stuck was Stoner Rock."

xref.title: Name Conflict with German Band
xref.body: Josh Homme's Gamma Ray project was short-lived as a potential long-term band due to a name conflict. A German power metal band already held the "Gamma Ray" name and initiated legal threats, forcing Homme to abandon the moniker for his new project. "His first thought was to resurrect gamma ray, but there was a problem. A German power metal band had dibs on that name and started making noises about legal action."

"Mark Lannigan was supposed to be the only other permanent person. He was offered the lead singer's spot, but he was way too busy, so he politely begged off."

"Josh still has an issue with his leg, and has been using a cane on occasion. And there was follow-up surgery in 2017 after he aggravated the injury shooting a video, but he's in a much better headspace than he was back in 2010."

xref.title: Ongoing Recording Series
xref.body: The Desert Sessions is a continuous series of recordings that started in the summer of 1997 and remains ongoing. The project originated from Josh Homme assembling friends at Rancho de la Luna to jam, returning to the desert to rekindle his musical inspiration. "The ultimate result has been an ongoing series of recordings called The Desert Sessions that continues even today."

xref.title: Originator of "Queens of the Stone Age" Name
xref.body: Goss coined the term "Queens of the Stone Age" as a studio nickname for Kyuss, which Josh Homme later adopted for his new band. "Whenever he was in the studio with the band, he would yell at Kias, calling them Queens of the Stone Age. As in you guys all sound like Queens of the Stone Age."

xref.title: Pink Duck Studios Owner
xref.body: Josh Homme owns and hosted an interview at Pink Duck Studios in Burbank, California. The studio's exterior from the front looked like an old corner store with a blocked door, but the back area, accessible via an alley, had a small parking area with a deck and picnic table. "Josh's Pink Duck Studios is within stupidly easy walking distance from the Burbank airport."

xref.title: Post-Surgery MRSA Infection
xref.body: After his near-fatal surgery in 2010, Josh Homme spent 13 days in the hospital but then contracted MRSA, a "Superbug" staff infection resistant to most antibiotics. This infection severely impacted his recovery, confining him to bed for four months with tubes in his leg, and for three of those months, he was unable to touch anyone due to the infection, which was particularly hard with his young daughter. "He was in hospital for 13 days before being discharged, but then it was discovered that he had contracted MRSA, the Superbug staff infection, that is resistant to almost every antibiotic available. Coding on the table was one thing, but it was the MRSA that really, really took a toll. He was confined to bed for four months with tubes in his leg. For three of those four months, he wasn't allowed to touch anybody because of the infection."

xref.title: Pre-Queens Foundation
xref.body: Kyuss is considered a pivotal "pre-Queens" band, representing a significant part of the early history for Josh Homme and Nick Oliveri and contributing to the "deep history" that preceded Queens of the Stone Age. "the story of Kias, the most important of all of the pre-Queen's bands"

xref.title: Producers for Chris Cornell's Solo Album – Launchpad for Other Gigs
xref.body: The group Eleven, comprising Elaine Johannes and Natasha Schneider, played a crucial role in producing Chris Cornell's debut solo record, *Euphoria Morning*. Their work on this album garnered them further producing gigs for notable artists like No Doubt and Josh Homme's Desert Session projects, connecting them to members of A Perfect Circle, Nine Inch Nails, Danzig, Marilyn Manson's band, and PJ Harvey. "Chris reliant on both of them to help produce his debut solo record Euphoria Morning... who, based on this work, got producing gigs for no doubt in Josh Hommie in the early days of his desert session projects."

xref.title: Queens of the Stone Age Debut Drummer
xref.body: Fredo Hernandez handled the drum duties for Queens of the Stone Age's self-titled debut album in 1998, as Josh Homme played most other instruments. "Josh played pretty much all the instruments with the exception of drums, which was handled by Fredo Hernandez from Kias."

xref.title: Reconciliation and Continued Collaboration
xref.body: Despite his past issues, Nick Oliveri eventually patched things up with Josh Homme, working together in the studio for background vocals on "Like Clockwork" and performing together on stage in 2014. Oliveri expressed a desire to rejoin Queens full-time, though this appears unlikely. "It took years, but things got patched up between him and Josh. They even worked in the studio together."

xref.title: Reconciliation with Nick Oliveri
xref.body: Despite his departure, Josh Homme and Nick Oliveri have reconciled their differences, even though Oliveri has not significantly rejoined the band's activities. "Nicola Vary has never re-entered the picture much, but he and Josh have long since reconciled."

xref.title: Supergroup Formation
xref.body: Them Crooked Vultures was formed as a supergroup, bringing together Josh Homme, Foo Fighters' Dave Grohl, and Led Zeppelin's bass player John Paul Jones. "Josh was one-third of them crooked vultures, a supergroup that featured Buddy Dave Grohl and Led Zeppelin bass player John Paul Jones."

xref.title: Supergroup Formation (Years Ago)
xref.body: The band formed after years of casual discussions among Dave Grohl (Foo Fighters), Josh Homme (Queens of the Stone Age), and John Paul Jones (Led Zeppelin) about creating music together. They finally decided to make it a reality. "After years of joking about forming a band together, Dave Grohl of the Fung Fighters, Josh Hommie of Queens of the Stone Age, and Led Zeppelin's John Paul Jones decided to make it happen with them crooked vultures."

xref.title: Sweet Stuff Foundation
xref.body: Josh Homme founded the Sweet Stuff Foundation, a charity dedicated to assisting musicians, producers, engineers, and their families who are facing hardships due to illness or disability. "And finally, Josh has something called the Sweet Stuff Foundation, which is a charity that helps up musicians, producers, engineers and their families when they run into times of illness and disability."

xref.title: Trent Reznor's Role in Josh Homme's Recovery
xref.body: During Josh Homme's recovery from his profound depression and near-death experience, Trent Reznor offered significant support, meeting with Homme for hours of conversation that Homme described as therapeutic and instrumental in his turnaround. "He credits Trent Rezner with helping him turn things around."
